key_insight: Perceptive Humanoid Parkour (PHP) shows that chaining a library of dynamic human motion clips via motion-matching, guided by perception, enables long-horizon, expressive, and robust parkour-style behaviors in humanoid agents.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between stable locomotion and highly dynamic, human-like parkour by addressing skill expressiveness, long-horizon composition, and perception-driven decision-making in complex environments.
method: Build a motion-matching skill library of dynamic human motions and retrieve best-fit clips at runtime.
Use a perception module to interpret terrain and obstacles, informing skill selection and transitions.
Employ a hierarchical planner/controller to chain retrieved skills into stable, long-horizon parkour trajectories.
impact: Provides a modular, scalable recipe for producing agile, human-like behaviors in humanoids, accelerating research on perception-informed dynamic tasks and easing integration between motion datasets and control systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: perception → motion matching (skill retrieval) → skill chaining → low-level controller
Sequence storyboard: a few frames showing chained parkour maneuvers (run → vault → landing)
Skill-library embedding scatterplot: nearest-neighbor matching for a sample query
Performance bar/line chart: success rate or robustness vs baseline controllers across varied terrains
paper_title: Perceptive Humanoid Parkour: Chaining Dynamic Human Skills via Motion Matching
paper_authors: Zhen Wu, Xiaoyu Huang, Lujie Yang, Yuanhang Zhang, Koushil Sreenath
